issues.legal_issue: A borrower has no right to obtain the benefit of a one-time settlement merely by requesting it.
material_facts: The borrower sought settlement of a loan account that had been classified as a non-performing asset.
No payment had been made toward that account before the borrower applied for settlement; a substantial payment was made only after the initial rejection.
The borrower and her husband regularly serviced two other loan accounts, indicating capacity to make payments.
The bank and its Settlement Advisory Committee considered the borrower’s financial position and concluded that the secured property was sufficient to recover the loan in full.
issues.conclusion: The benefit of a one-time settlement cannot be claimed as a matter of right and is subject to the scheme’s eligibility criteria and the bank’s assessment of recovery prospects. The bank may refuse settlement where the borrower can pay or the full debt can be recovered from secured property.
issues.legal_principle: The one-time settlement scheme makes relief conditional on eligibility and provides for examination of applications by a Settlement Advisory Committee, including consideration of recovery efforts and whether the possibility of recovery has been minimized. Under the scheme and applicable Reserve Bank guidelines, a borrower is not entitled to settlement as of right; a bank may rely on its commercial judgment where the borrower can pay or the debt can be recovered from secured property. No earlier cases are relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: borrower_seeks_ots and (eligibility_criteria_unmet or borrower_can_pay or full_recovery_from_security_likely)

predicates.borrower_seeks_ots: A borrower applies to a lender for relief under a one-time settlement arrangement.
predicates.eligibility_criteria_unmet: The borrower does not satisfy one or more eligibility conditions of the settlement arrangement.
predicates.borrower_can_pay: The lender's assessment indicates that the borrower has the capacity to pay the debt under the loan account.
predicates.full_recovery_from_security_likely: The lender's assessment indicates that the full debt can be recovered by enforcing security provided for the loan.
predicates.borrower_has_no_automatic_ots_entitlemen: The borrower is not entitled to obtain one-time settlement relief merely by requesting it.

issues.definition: When a borrower seeks settlement and is ineligible, able to pay, or subject to a likelihood of full recovery from security, the borrower has no automatic entitlement to settlement.

issues.legal_issue: A court exercising constitutional writ jurisdiction cannot direct a bank to grant one-time settlement relief or positively consider such relief contrary to the scheme’s eligibility requirements and the bank’s supported recovery assessment.
material_facts: The borrower sought a writ directing the bank to provide one-time settlement relief.
The bank and its Settlement Advisory Committee found that the borrower did not qualify and that recovery in full remained possible from the secured property.
Recovery proceedings were pending, and the bank had considered the borrower’s financial position and the available security.
The High Court directed the bank to positively consider the settlement application, treating the possibility of recovery as illusory because recovery proceedings had remained pending.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its jurisdiction by directing the bank to positively consider or grant settlement relief. Its order was set aside; the decision whether to grant relief was for the bank to make under the scheme and in its commercial judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Article 226 does not authorize a writ of mandamus compelling a bank to grant one-time settlement relief contrary to the scheme’s eligibility criteria. The scheme and applicable Reserve Bank guidelines leave the decision to the bank’s competent process and commercial judgment; where the bank reasonably assesses that the borrower can pay or that full recovery from secured property is possible, it may refuse settlement. The pendency of recovery proceedings alone does not establish that recovery is illusory. No earlier cases are relied on for this ruling.

predicates.constitutional_writ_seeking_ots_mandamus: A borrower brings a constitutional writ proceeding seeking an order requiring a bank to provide or positively consider one-time settlement relief.
predicates.eligibility_criteria_unmet: The borrower does not satisfy one or more eligibility conditions of the settlement arrangement.
predicates.bank_assesses_full_recovery_likely: The bank, after considering the relevant circumstances, assesses that the full debt can likely be recovered from the borrower or secured property.
predicates.court_cannot_compel_ots_relief: A court cannot require the bank to provide one-time settlement relief contrary to the scheme and the bank's supported assessment.

issues.definition: In a constitutional writ proceeding seeking compelled settlement relief, ineligibility or the bank’s supported assessment that full recovery is likely means the court cannot compel that relief.

issues.legal_issue: A bank’s rejection of a settlement application does not breach natural justice where the borrower was given an opportunity to be heard before the decision.
material_facts: The Settlement Advisory Committee gave the borrower a personal hearing before deciding her settlement application.
The bank and the committee made a considered decision rejecting the application.
The High Court proceeded on the factual premise that the borrower had not been given an opportunity to be heard.
issues.conclusion: The rejection was not in breach of natural justice because the borrower had in fact been heard.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the requirement of a fair opportunity to be heard and found that it had been met on the facts. It relied on no statutory provision or earlier case for this specific finding.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_ots_rejection: A borrower challenges a bank's rejection of a one-time settlement application in a writ proceeding.
predicates.borrower_heard_before_decision: The bank or its decision-making committee gives the borrower an opportunity to be heard before rejecting the application.
predicates.ots_rejection_not_in_breach_of_natural_j: The rejection does not breach natural justice on the ground that the borrower was denied an opportunity to be heard.

issues.definition: In a writ challenge to a settlement rejection, if the borrower was heard before the decision, the rejection is not in breach of natural justice on that ground.
